_doc: Rules layer for build_dc_delay.py. HAND-EDIT. Every instrument carries source + date + a tag (HARD = statute/order/date on record; PARTIAL = sourced range, exact month ours; ESTIMATE = ours). PROVISIONAL until the 2026-11-06 rules research (raw/state_local_rules.md) is folded in.

basis.note: MW are converted to IT-equivalent before any sum: facility (and utility/grid load requests) ÷1.2, on-site generation nameplate ÷1.5, unknown basis treated as facility.

tags.facility: PARTIAL — UBS CoreWeave initiation (themes/ai-datacenter-power.md, 2026-09-22 block): gross facility load 'can be 10-25% larger than IT Load'; Bernstein 2026-10-02: +19 IT-GW ≈ ~25 facility GW (×1.32). 1.2 sits inside 1.10-1.32.
tags.grid: ESTIMATE — utility load requests treated as facility load.
tags.gen: ESTIMATE — on-site generation is sized for redundancy (N+1) and derating; 1.5 = facility 1.2 × 1.25 redundancy.
tags.unknown: ESTIMATE — most press MW for campuses are power/facility figures; treated as facility.

lead_tags.air_permit: PARTIAL — Capstone internal deck: ~12 months to build the on-site plant once the air permit issues (Stargate Abilene example).
lead_tags.interconnection: ESTIMATE — months from a reopened large-load approval to energization for a phase whose shell is already being built.
lead_tags.new_license: PARTIAL — Capstone internal deck: 18-month build ('prazo de obra 18 meses').

base.label: Base
base.blurb: Pauses already in force run to their likely end (TX through the 2027 session, OR and NY to Jul-27); pledges and bills stay off. Unknown approvals count as missing only for phases not yet started.

bear.label: Bear (post-election)
bear.blurb: The deck's case: winners' pledges become pauses (TX to the Sep-1 effective date, OH and GA 6 months, NM) and VA SB 843 passes. Unknown air-permit status counts as missing for phases not yet energized.

stress.label: Stress
stress.blurb: Every pause runs to its long end (TX Dec-27, OH/GA/NM ~12 months), NY's one-year bill is signed, local moratoria are renewed once. Unknown air-permit and interconnection status counts as missing for phases not yet energized. An ERCOT interconnection agreement no longer protects a phase (ERCOT: even Base Load still needs verification).

TX.dc_stance: Pledged: 'When I am governor I will issue a moratorium — a ban — on all data center approvals until laws can be passed by the Legislature' (Oct-22 video); campaign: applies to 'any new permits'. Also: end sales-tax exemption, ban NDAs, union labour, household bill/water protections. Works with a Democratic House; Senate stays Republican (~19-12, per Luminix).
TX.source: https://kfoxtv.com/news/local/gina-hinojosa-won-the-governors-race-what-happens-to-texas-data-centers-now-11-04-2026 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections (revision 1384082438, read 2026-11-06; results provisional/uncertified) ; FundaAI 2026-11-04 (takes office Jan 19) via _wiki\themes\ai-datacenter-power.md

OH.dc_stance: 'Conditional moratorium' on NEW data centers: proceed only if developers meet conditions — 100% union labour, environmental standards, community-benefit agreements, cover all utility costs (statenews 2026-07-27, 4 named) + no NDAs, own energy (same article); Luminix 2026-11-05 lists six incl. incentive clawbacks and brownfield siting. No draft executive order published; Republicans kept both chambers.

GA.dc_stance: Temporary statewide pause on state approvals for NEW data centers 'until consumer protections are established'; no end date, mechanism or exemptions stated (SemiAnalysis 11-01; WTVM 11-05). Luminix (secondary): length 'one month, six months, or longer'; not a permanent halt. PSC flipped to 3-2 Democratic.

NV.dc_stance: Pause on NEW data-center TAX ABATEMENTS until a GOED audit shows commitments are met; ban wasteful evaporative cooling; 'not one penny' of cost shift. No construction/permit moratorium pledged.

IA.dc_stance: Stricter conditions, no pause (SemiAnalysis 11-01: 'stopped short of calling for a pause'); would end incentives and make DCs pay own costs. Opponent Lahn (R) backed a moratorium — he lost.

KS.dc_stance: Not researched (web-search budget exhausted). Kansas local ballot bans passed 11-03 (El Dorado, Emporia, Ottawa).

NM.dc_stance: Day-one executive order: moratorium on NEW large-scale data-center projects until protections are in place and any necessary rulemaking is complete; 8-point plan (own renewables, closed-loop water, union labour, decommissioning bonds, clawbacks). Pre-election said 'I don't have the power to stop Project Jupiter'.

AZ.dc_stance: Against a statewide moratorium; three-year freeze on new DC tax-program applications already in law (Jul-2026 to Jun-2029); wants DCs to pay for water.

PA.dc_stance: Conditions, no moratorium: EO 2026-05 (Aug-18) GRID requirements + local approval before DEP permits for >25 MW; backs HB 2650. Garrity (R, pause while municipalities update rules) lost.

OR.dc_stance: Supports a statewide moratorium; DEQ air/water permit hold and state-land pause both to 2027-07-01; reforms in the 2027 session.

NY.dc_stance: EO 62 (2026-07-14) DEC permit pause for >=50 MW pending a GEIS ('up to a year'); declined to sign the legislature's 1-year >=20 MW RDCD Act (action due by end-Dec-2026; veto expected by law firms).

IL.dc_stance: No moratorium; stopped processing new sales-tax-exemption agreements from 2026-07-01; wants DCs to pay full energy/water cost.

OK.dc_stance: Open to DCs, opposes a pause, wants developers to pay their own way (SemiAnalysis 11-01). Munson (D, day-one moratorium) lost.

MI.dc_stance: Not verified (web-search budget exhausted). Both 2026 US Senate candidates called for DC moratoriums (SemiAnalysis 11-01) — federal office, no power to enact.

WI.dc_stance: Not verified (web-search budget exhausted). Statewide moratorium bill SB1061/AB1099 died 2026-03-23 (tracker).

MN.dc_stance: Not verified (web-search budget exhausted). Statewide permitting-moratorium bill SF4298/HF4888 died 2026-05 (tracker).

IN.dc_stance: No 2026 governor race. No state pause; restrictions are county/city level (~1/3 of counties by Jul-2026).

VA.dc_stance: No 2026 governor race. Has not backed a statewide moratorium; EO 22 (2026-09-18) 'Data Center Accountability Framework' — conditions, no pause. The deck's quote ('é uma escolha local') was not found in a primary.

LA.dc_stance: No 2026 governor race. No state pause found; local pauses only (New Orleans).
LA.source: relatórios bons\2026_11_06_amigo_felipe_gw_atrasa_pausas_estaduais.html ; Moratorium Nation local inventory (Michael J. Bommarito, CC-BY-4.0), https://mjbommar.github.io/moratorium-data-2026/data/moratorium_inventory.csv, cohort 2026-11-05

MO.dc_stance: No 2026 governor race; SemiAnalysis left MO out of its tiers ('large Republican majorities and supportive governors'). Local: St. Charles County/City.

SC.dc_stance: Not researched (web-search budget exhausted); no state pause found in the tracker.

TN.dc_stance: Not researched (web-search budget exhausted); local pauses only (Nashville to 2026-12-01; Memphis proposed).
TN.source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_United_States_gubernatorial_elections (revision 1384082438, read 2026-11-06; results provisional/uncertified) ; Moratorium Nation local inventory (Michael J. Bommarito, CC-BY-4.0), https://mjbommar.github.io/moratorium-data-2026/data/moratorium_inventory.csv, cohort 2026-11-05

AL.dc_stance: Not researched (web-search budget exhausted); AL 2026 law limited DC tax abatements (HB399), no pause.

FL.dc_stance: 'Less critical of data centers … did not support a statewide pause' (NewsNation/SciAm summaries 11-04/05).

instruments.note: No mechanism, end date or exemptions stated; PSC-approved contracts (e.g. Project Camellia) the likeliest carve-out.

instruments.note: Prefiled by Sen. Perry; would bar local and state approvals for NEW DCs 2027-07-01 → 2030-07-01; 'vested right' for projects in process under discussion. In the deck's bear case; the rules research rates it stress-only.

semianalysis_local.source: SemiAnalysis 2026-11-01, restating its 2026-09-15 moratorium piece (~1.5 GW delayed of ~20 GW inside local restrictions)

wfs_tx_held.source: Wells Fargo (Revich et al.), 'Texas Policy Reset Adds Timing Risk to 20-30% of the Data Center Power Pipeline', 2026-11-04
wfs_tx_held.caveat: About 3 GW of its ~37 GW recip and CAT-turbine trackers sits on Texas projects 'now seemingly on hold' (generation nameplate). WFS: several entries undisclosed, so these are floors. Generation ÷1.5 to IT-eq is our basis factor.

context.text: Both Abbott (June-10 directive) and Hinojosa want the 2027 Legislature to end the data-center sales-tax exemption. Cost, not delay.
context.why_no_delay: Would take effect with 2027 legislation (Sep-1 default). Raises cost (~7% on equipment where state sales tax applies — The Information 2026-08-02 via wiki); does not block approvals.

context.text: No pause. EO 22 (signed 2026-09-18, effective immediately): bans state-agency NDAs on DC projects; >=25 MW DCs barred from VEDP Business Ready Sites, expedited permitting and similar discretionary programs; Eastern Virginia Groundwater Management Area designated a cooling-water scarcity area; DEQ to propose noise and backup-generation rules within 180 days; cost-allocation work with SCC/PJM (assign PJM backstop costs to causative DCs); by-right elimination / >25 MW local-approval requested from the 2027 General Assembly.
context.why_no_delay: Standing conditions; loss of expedited permitting lengthens state reviews by an unquantified amount. DEQ rule proposals due ~Mar-2027 (180 days).

context.text: Temporary moratorium on local approvals of data centers until the earlier of fulfilment of pending DC interconnection requests or 2028-07-01.
context.why_no_delay: Continued to 2027 in House Rules (2026-02-06). If passed in the 2027 session it would take effect Jul-1-2027 (Virginia default; inferred) and end by Jul-1-2028 at the latest. Same veto logic as SB 843 → not in base.
context.source: Moratorium Nation state tracker (state_legislation.csv, id va-hb1515), https://mjbommar.github.io/moratorium-data-2026/data/state_legislation.csv

context.text: DeWine paused NEW approvals/applications under the data-center sales-tax exemption (R.C. 122.175). Cost, not delay.
context.why_no_delay: Runs until DeWine leaves office (Jan-2027) per Luminix; Acton inherits it and wants to reduce, not eliminate, incentives (SemiAnalysis 11-01). Statutory cut introduced 2026-11-05, not passed (Luminix).

context.text: New 3-2 Democratic PSC majority plans an 'affordability docket' reviewing DC cost allocation; independent review of Georgia Power's DC billing methodology already ordered. No pause on certification announced. Commissioner Hubbard: not his 'power or interest to stop data center expansion'.
context.why_no_delay: Seating date of new commissioners not stated in the source (January 2027 inferred). Cost/terms, not a hold.

context.text: Not a pause. For DCs >25 MW peak: DEP will not issue permits until GRID requirements are met (binding consent order) AND local approvals are obtained; without a consent order DEP waits for local + water approvals before even starting review and issues all permits together; DCs removed from PA Permit Fast Track; NDAs banned.
context.why_no_delay: Standing regime (no expiry). SemiAnalysis does not count it as a pause ('a moratorium expires, whereas a conditional permitting regime does not'). Delay = time to obtain local approval + GRID consent; Shapiro re-elected so it persists.

context.text: Codifies GRID requirements (and could tighten tax benefits).
context.why_no_delay: Passed House 134-68 on 2026-06-24; Republican Senate has not acted. The 2025-26 session ends 2026-11-30, so it dies unless passed in the lame duck (inferred from PA's two-year session rule) and must be reintroduced in 2027. HB2496 (municipal 180-day pause authority, passed House 201-1) and SB1345 (up to 18-month municipal moratoria) also pending.
context.source: relatórios bons\2026_11_01_ENC_The_Datacenter_Backlash_Goes_Bipartisan_Next_Weeks_Midterms_and_the_2028_Buildout_email.html ; Moratorium Nation state tracker (pa-hb2496, pa-sb1345)

context.text: Three-year moratorium on NEW applications/certifications to the state Computer Data Center tax-relief program (HB 4168 s.31, Laws 2026 ch.140). Does not pause construction, siting or local permitting.
Stopped processing new data-center sales-tax-exemption agreements from 2026-07-01 (Pritzker June directive). Cost only.
Pledged pause on NEW data-center tax abatements until a GOED audit confirms commitments. No permit or construction pause.
context.why_no_delay: Ford takes office Jan-2027; abatement pause open-ended ('not to say the breaks will never resume'). Cost only → Nevada should NOT carry a state permit pause (the deck outlines NV as a state-pause state).

context.text: State agencies pause unapproved easements, rights-of-way, leases, land-use permits and sales/transfers of STATE-OWNED property for DC projects.
context.why_no_delay: Directive 2026-09-08 runs through 2027-07-01 (SemiAnalysis 09-15). SemiAnalysis: no forecast impact (bites before site control).

context.text: Gov. Beshear's Executive Order 2026-494 (signed 2026-08-06): developers must file an energy plan with the Energy and Environment Cabinet showing ratepayers are protected; the state may deny permits on air or water grounds; no avoidance of state and local taxes. Siting stays local.
context.why_no_delay: Conditions, not a moratorium (Beshear: the order 'doesn't say yes to any data center' but says no to those that fail the requirements). TeraWulf's Muskie site says it will comply (8-K 2026-10-05). Could slow a permit case by case; not modelled as a pause.
